label: rare early-copy-phase feature (recall 0-3, often input 2/v/i), no specific trigger found
explanation: Extremely sparse: 89 dev steps, about 0.0014% of steps. 95% of the mass is in the delimiter step and the first few copy steps (recall_idx 0-3). The input there is usually 2, v, i or <DEL>, and the sequences tend to be digit-rich and often contain q or repeated letters. The feature almost never fires in the original phase and never at t<4. Those conditions cover about 88% of activations but match about 650k steps (precision about 0.0001). Adding conditions on q, digit count or the input being 2 lifts precision only to about 0.003 and loses most recall. I found no predicate that picks out the rare firing contexts, so the activations look like the sparse tail of some distributed hidden-state direction. Magnitude is narrow (0.10-0.17), and I did not find what modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+2.89), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+2.83), out_tok=r (+2.54), out_tok=i (+2.47), in_tok=2 (+2.24), prev_tok=m (+1.79). Lower it: in_first=0 (-1.57), to_go=1 (-1.53), n_digits=0 (-1.46), to_go=2 (-1.39).
